learn.b.title: An AI helper, if you want one.
learn.b.body: Off by default. Connect your own AI app through MCP for Unity. Its edits appear as undoable AI: steps. You choose whether to share pictures, one at a time or until Unity closes.
learn.b.alt: The AI helper shows the setup steps, the control set to Off, and what the helper can access.
opt.1.b: Crunch shrinks the download but smears colour and detail, and turning it off makes the avatar a little bigger. Avistry warns you and has a Turn off Crunch button.
opt.2.b: A JPG blurs detail and cannot hold transparency. Avistry flags JPG sources and always saves a PNG.
opt.3.b: Sizes like 1024 or 2048 use less memory than odd sizes, which can look soft. Avistry tells you when a size is off.
opt.4.b: The Box filter blurs a texture when it is seen from far away. VRChat recommends Kaiser, and there is a Use Kaiser button in Advanced mode.
opt.5.b: Colour images need sRGB on, and data images like masks need it off. Normal maps need the Normal map type. Wrong settings wash out colour or break an effect, and Fix N image settings corrects them.
opt.6.t: Same import settings on the new PNG
opt.6.b: The saved PNG copies the original's max size, compression and other import settings, so it behaves like the file it replaces.
opt.7.b: On colour textures laid out by the part’s UVs, the empty space around pieces is filled with their edge colours, so mipmaps do not pull the background into seams.
opt.8.b: Finds empty slots, extra materials that draw a part twice and slow the avatar, pink shaders and missing images, hidden parts included.

mat.title: Material
mat.c.tint.b: Shifts the colour of the whole material, on top of the texture. Handy to try a colour before you repaint.
mat.c.glow.b: Makes eyes, trim or lines give off their own light, so they stand out in dark worlds.
mat.c.rim.b: A bright edge along the outline of a part, so it stands out from the background.
mat.c.matcap.b: A ready-made shine laid over the part, for a glossy, reflective look on skin, latex or gems.
mat.c.shadow.b: Picks the colour of the shaded side. A warm or coloured shadow makes toon shading look richer.
mat.c.outline.b: Choose the colour and width of the line around a part, when your shader has an outline.
mat.c.metal.b: Make a surface read as polished metal. Poiyomi needs its PBR section on; lilToon Lite has no metal.
mat.c.glitter.b: Add sparkling specks and choose their colour. Your shader decides how they move.
safety.lead: Avistry has its own edit history. Saving textures creates new files and can create a material copy.
undo.title: Go back through Avistry edits.

files.title: Your files stay safe.
files.body: New textures, saved edits and material copies go in Assets/Avistry/Output.
card.title: Catch problems before you upload.
card.body: Scan for missing materials, broken shaders and wrong texture settings. Avistry offers a fix when it can safely make one.
card.head: Material check on the workshop avatar
card.alt: The Check materials panel flags an empty material slot and a texture import setting, with buttons to select or fix them.
card.also: Also done every time you save

ft.meta.title: Avistry features | Avatar texture editing in Unity
ft.meta.description: Select, recolour and paint avatar textures in Unity. Preview reusable layers, save drafts and share editable style packs.
ft.title: Every tool in action.
ft.lead: Short videos and screenshots from Unity show how to select, paint, recolour and save an avatar edit.
workflow.title: Gradient in the Scene view
workflow.video: Select the enamel, then drag a gradient across it in the Scene view. The metal rim keeps its colour.
workflow.limit.title: Choose where to edit
workflow.limit.body: Pick pieces or faces in Limit. Use Paint selected or Gradient on selected to keep the edit in that area.
workflow.join.title: Reach the part you want
workflow.join.body: Isolate edited parts hides covering objects while you work. Smooth across joins lets supported round and stamp tips follow the model across UV seams.
workflow.keys.title: Switch tools in Scene
workflow.keys.body: Use the overlay to switch between Select, Recolour and Paint. Use the arrow keys on a focused choice or hold Shift while scrolling over it.
reopen.title: Keep editing or share a style.
reopen.draft.title: Drafts
reopen.draft.body: Use Save draft to keep your layers in the project. Find them later with Browse drafts.
reopen.template.title: Templates
reopen.template.body: Open Templates in Paint to preview reusable layers. While previewing, press Escape to return to the filtered list.
reopen.pack.title: Style packs
reopen.pack.body: Use Pack and Share in Advanced Save to export editable changes and added artwork. Recipients use their own avatar assets and can preview matching edits before opening a draft.

mat.lead2: A material controls how a part responds to light. Quick material puts frequently used settings for Poiyomi, lilToon and supported Unity shaders together in Recolour.
mat.how.1: Pick a part and open Quick material in Recolour.
mat.how.2: Change a control and watch the part update in Scene view.
mat.how.3: The sliders change a copy of the material, made with one click. The original stays as it was.
map.lead2: Two maps that give a flat texture depth, made for you in seconds. There is a toon face shadow map for anime faces too.
map.ao.what: Soft shading where light hardly reaches: creases, under the hair, between feathers and fingers. Flat toon textures get depth without painting shadows by hand.
map.ao.f1: Baked from the model in its current pose, on your graphics card.
map.ao.f2: Clothing and hair can shade the part under them too.
map.ao.f3: Added as a Multiply layer: fade it with Layer opacity or keep it off places with a mask.
map.ao.alt2: An ambient occlusion preview with shadows along the raised trim, alongside the bake controls.
map.normal.what: Fake bumps made from the light and dark details of the texture: stitches, fabric, scales, hammered metal. Light catches them as if they were really raised.
map.normal.f1: Strength and Smoothness set how deep and how fine the bumps are.
map.normal.f2: Keeps the bumps of the material's own normal map and adds the new ones on top, if you like.
map.normal.f3: Saved as a separate PNG. Apply to material puts it in the normal-map slot.
demo.scope.title: Turn a selection into an edit
demo.scope.body: Start a Paint layer or a gradient that stays inside the selected pieces or faces.
demo.wand.title: Pick by colour
demo.wand.body: Pick by colour with the Wand. Make matches a selection, or show and hide matching areas on a layer mask.
demo.fill.title: Fill by colour or area
demo.fill.body: Fill an area of connected, similar colours, the selection or the whole texture. Close gaps keeps the fill from leaking through small breaks.
demo.stops.title: Edit gradient stops
demo.stops.body: Move or remove colour and opacity stops, pick recent colours and copy or paste colour codes.
demo.blends.body: Group layers, merge compatible Paint layers with editable strokes, or add up to four ordered blends with separate strengths.
demo.masks.title: Create and paint masks
demo.masks.body: Pick a shader mask slot or paint a hide/reveal mask on a layer.
demo.material.title: Start a texture or copy settings
demo.material.body: Create a paintable texture on a supported Unity Standard material. Use Advanced Copy to review and transfer supported settings between materials.
demo.drag.title: Drop a target or saved edit
demo.drag.body: Drop a part, material or saved edit onto Avistry. The drop hint shows what the tool can open.
demo.standard.title: Quick material on Unity Standard
demo.standard.body: The Recolour tab shows the settings the shader supports, including Tint and Glow on Unity Standard.
demo.animation.title: Review Poiyomi animated settings
demo.animation.body: Quick material shows which settings remain animated on a locked Poiyomi material. Before you clear an Animated mark on an editable copy, it warns that toggles or sliders using that setting can stop working when you lock it again.

studio.title: Edit textures in Unity.
studio.intro: Select a surface, paint on the model, and keep every edit in layers.
studio.opening.hint: Scroll to see how it’s made
studio.opening.original.title: Start with a blank material
studio.opening.original.body: The unedited headset has a plain grey texture. The mesh and camera stay in place through every step.
studio.opening.layers.title: Build the design in layers
studio.opening.layers.body: Lay down the colour, then add the artwork on its own layer.
studio.opening.texture.title: Add surface detail
studio.opening.texture.body: Build grain and wear into the texture so each part has its own finish.
studio.opening.ao.title: Bake contact shadows
studio.opening.ao.body: Ambient occlusion deepens seams and the spots where pieces meet.
studio.opening.normals.title: Give the pattern depth
studio.opening.normals.body: Bake a normal map so the fine pattern catches the light.
studio.opening.metal.title: Finish the material
studio.opening.metal.body: Adjust gloss and metal to bring out highlights while keeping the other surfaces matte.
studio.opening.alt: The same headset in Unity at each stage of the material edit
studio.hero.alt: The headset with the edited texture
studio.select.title: Select where the edit goes.
studio.select.body: Preview a selection before you click. The mesh and texture show the same pieces. Return to a part to pick up its selection again.
studio.select.gesture.title: Select and switch meshes
studio.select.gesture.body: Drag a box or lasso around the earcup. Select the headband, then return to the earcup to see its selection restored.
studio.select.uv.note: Click a piece, drag a box, or draw a lasso to choose an area.
studio.select.part.note: Select the pieces on a part or inside a UV tile.
studio.select.topology.note: Pick faces, follow loops, or select edges and vertices.
studio.select.colour.note: Pick a base colour to find matching areas in the texture.
studio.select.paint.note: The brush stroke stays on the selected piece.
studio.paint.title: Paint on the model.
studio.paint.body: Brush, fill or drag a gradient inside the selected area.
studio.paint.more.body: Mirror a stroke, restrict the paint area, erase on a layer, or fill a region by colour. Work on the 3D surface or on its texture.
studio.layers.title: Build the finish in layers.
studio.layers.body: Choose a material and follow its layers from the original texture to the finished surface.
studio.layers.more.body: Clip paint to the layer below, stack blend modes with individual strengths, or merge layers. Compatible paint layers can keep their editable strokes.
studio.layer.base.note: The original texture before any edits.
studio.layer.shell.note: Fill each selected piece with its own base colour.
studio.layer.gradient.note: Shape the colour using editable gradient stops.
studio.layer.print.note: Paint waves and cherry blossoms on a separate layer.
studio.layer.paint.note: Build up fine bristle marks and leather grain.
studio.layer.mask.note: Hide parts of the brush texture without deleting the strokes.
studio.layer.detail.note: Add repeated stitches, fabric texture and fine metal brushing.
studio.layer.finish.note: Bake the painted detail into a normal map, then tune metal and gloss.
studio.colour.title: Match a reference colour.
studio.colour.body: Choose a reference colour to recolour the selected leather panels.
studio.colour.more.body: Adjust hue, saturation and brightness, or use a gradient map to map colours to the texture’s light and dark areas.
studio.maps.title: Bake shadows and surface detail.
studio.maps.body: Bake ambient occlusion from the mesh and make a normal map from texture detail.
studio.unity.bake: Bake maps and apply a normal map in Unity
studio.maps.metal.body: Turn texture detail into surface relief. Compare the material with the normal map on and off.
studio.maps.motion: Moving light across a surface with a normal map
studio.maps.compatible: Use generated maps with supported Unity Standard, Poiyomi and lilToon materials.
studio.maps.compare: Compare the material with and without the normal map
studio.maps.more.body: Make a material copy in Quick material, copy supported settings with Advanced Copy, and use compatible Unity Standard, lilToon and Poiyomi materials.
studio.save.title: Save and share
studio.save.body: Save a new texture and material, reopen an editable draft, or share a style pack with just the edits.
studio.save.alt: The Avistry Save panel showing export options
studio.save.more.body: Save a template to reuse your settings. Reopen a draft to keep working, or step back through Avistry’s edit history.
studio.learn.title: Learn in Unity.

studio.material.quick.title: Quick material

studio.material.base.note: A soft finish keeps the painted detail visible with broad highlights.

studio.save.drafts.body: Browse unfinished edits and continue with their layers intact.
studio.save.templates.body: Save the settings and layers to start another edit.
studio.save.pack.body: Share editable layers and added artwork. The recipient supplies the original textures and model.
